correctness.rationale: The characteristic-two open-neighbor map is J_m⊗I+I⊗J_n+E (J_s all-ones), with E the symmetric distinguished-corner swap; the two diagonal self-terms cancel. For odd side s the all-ones tail has coordinate sum one and splits from the tail kernel; for even s>=4 it lies in the tail kernel and splits by taking a complement there and adjoining a tail unit vector to the core. At s=2 the whole space is distinguished. This yields cores of size 2,3,4 respectively with the right sum functional and distinguished coordinates; J kills the remainder and E kills any tensor sector containing that remainder. Noncore sectors therefore contribute only one-side rank-one idempotents or square-zero maps and zero operators. The six core profiles were independently rebuilt and checked by polynomial nullities and annihilator identities. In particular both mixed cores have p-nullities (3,6,6,6) for p=z³+z+1, giving exactly one cyclic p² module, not two simple p modules. All dimensions and the tail multiplicities agree, including (2,2), e=2 and o=3. Extension to F_q is scalar extension; if p splits there, the companion-block description is still valid as defined. A root of p generates F_8^×, and z^7-1 is square-free, so p occurs in z^7-1 but p² first divides z^14-1. The kernel at update seven gives states of exact period seven, and a cyclic generator gives exact period fourteen. The rank table follows by taking powers on the nilpotent and invertible summands. First entry occurs when the nilpotent coordinate first vanishes, so entry by k counts q^(r+mn-r_k); all nilpotent choices over each recurrent phase account for d q^(mn-r) per orbit. The reported P_d follow by fixed-space dimensions and the exact primitive counts by divisor inversion, including one 7-cycle and four 14-cycles on the 2×3 binary board. For comparison the intact operator squares to zero in even–even parity, is idempotent in odd–odd parity, and in mixed parity splits into a square-zero component and an involution. Its exact periods cannot exceed two.
residual_risks: The all-size conclusion depends on the tensor splitting, not finite sampling of boards. The classification does not extend as stated to more edits, closed neighborhoods or other characteristics.

value.rationale: A single symmetric bond in a standard network changes the possible recurrence periods from at most two to seven and fourteen uniformly across mixed sizes. A uniform decomposition into a small active core and passive sectors explains this, records sharp exceptions, and predicts more than just the presence of a long orbit: maximum transient, exact counts and basins over every characteristic-two finite field. This is an exact perturbation benchmark rather than a claim that fourteen cycles are new in XOR dynamics.
residual_risks: Applications are to this synchronous linear update model; no analogous behavior is established for nonlinear dynamics, multiple bond perturbations, or empirical networks.
